The captioned appeal is filed by
the injured/claimant questioning quantum and negligence in MVC.No.939/2012.
2.  The Tribunal in absence of income proof assessed the income notionally at Rs.3,000/- and awarded Rs.40,320/- under the head of future loss of earnings due to permanent physical disability.
Tribunal in all has awarded Rs.1,48,340/- with interest at the rate of 9% NC: 2024:KHC-K:9814 from the date of petition till its realization.

Further, referring to the charge sheet materials, the Tribunal has attributed negligence in the ratio of 30:70 on the driver of the goods truck bearing No.MA-13-AX 2339 and the driver of the offending truck bearing No.KA-36-A-2976 who had illegally parked the truck in the middle of the road.

3. The Tribunal having apportioned the negligence dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.4/New India Insurance company on the ground it is not liable to pay 70% of compensation since the inmates of the goods vehicle were traveling as gratuitous passengers.

The claim petition was in fact allowed against the owner of the offending truck i.e. respondent No.3 and 30% liability was fastened on respondents 1 and 2 primarily fixing the liability on respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company Limited.
4. The present appeal is filed questioning the quantum as well as the negligence.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the appellant /claimant and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4/New India Assurance Company limited.
FINDING ON NEGLIGENCE:

6. This Court in MFA.No.202567/2019 considering the arguments advanced by the counsel appearing for the claimants and the counsel appearing for both the Insurance Companies has after meticulous examination of the material on record and on an elaborate discussion held that both the drivers of the truck were negligent and therefore, attributed negligence in the ratio of 50:50.
Accordingly, negligence is attributed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident.

Further more, since the truck bearing No. MH- 13-AX-2339 was used in violation of the policy conditions permitting 30 passengers to travel in the goods vehicle,
Respondent No.3, who is the owner of the truck bearing NC: 2024:KHC-K:9814 No.
MH-13-AX-2339 is liable to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company who is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA.36/A.2976 which was illegally parked is jointly and severally liable along with respondent No.1 to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

FINDING ON QUANTUM:
7.
The appellant contended that she has suffered fracture of lower end of right radius and also cut lacerated wound over skull and contusion over chest.
The Tribunal in absence of income proof assessed the income of the appellant herein at Rs.3,000/- and has awarded Rs.40,320/-.
This Court is of the view that the income assessed at Rs.3,000/- is on the lower side.

In absence of income proof, this Court is inclined to accept the income pleaded in the claim petition i.e. Rs.6,000/- since the income chart prepared by the KSLSA notionally prescribes the income at Rs.6,500/-.

Thus,
taking the income at Rs.6,000/-, disability determined by the Tribunal at 8% NC:
2024:KHC-K:9814 and applying the multiplier 13, compensation payable under the future loss of earnings works out to (Rs.6,000x8/100x12x13)Rs.74,880/-.
8.

The amount awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering Rs.30,000/-, towards medical expenses Rs.20,900/-, attendant charges Rs.20,000/-, conveyance charges Rs.20,000/-, food and nourishment Rs.10,000/- does not warrant interference.
However, having regard to the gravity of injuries, this Court deems it fit to award Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Tribunal has erred in not awarding compensation under the head of loss of earnings during the laid up period.
Considering the period of treatment as three months, Rs.18,000/- is awarded.

9. In summary, the total compensation re- determined by this Court under various heads is as follows:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.

3  1. Pain and sufferings Rs.30,000/-

2 . Future loss of earnings Rs.74,880/-
 NC: 2024:KHC-K:9814

3. Medical expenses Rs.20,900/-
 4. Laid up period (6,000x3) Rs.18,000/-
 5. Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/-
 6. Attendant charges Rs.20,000/-
 7. Food and Nourishment Rs.10,000/-
 8. Conveyance charges Rs.20,000/-
The total compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.2,23,780/- as against Rs.1,48,340/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the claimants are held entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.75,440/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

11. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
(iii) The appellant is held entitled to  enhanced compensation of Rs.75,440/- which shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization;
(iv) The negligence is fixed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles.

Respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally held liable to deposit 50% of compensation awarded and balance 50% shall be paid by respondent No.3/Owner of the offending vehicle i.e.
